Title: SeaKeepers Monthly Morningside Cleanup
Content: Come join SeaKeepers for our monthly cleanup at Morningside Park! Weather permitting, we will cleanup all along the waterside with the option to kayak or paddleboard to the nearby Picnic Islands. Make sure to visit the SeaKeepers tent for check-in, and then instructions and a safety-briefing will be given to the group! You are welcome to join us on foot or by paddle! SeaKeepers will NOT be providing kayaks. You may bring your own kayak or paddleboard, or kayak and paddleboard rentals are available from Morningside Watersports at a 30% discount when you mention you’re with SeaKeepers! You will be able to paddle across Biscayne Bay to the nearby Picnic Islands to clean up there as well. A SeaKeeper will show you where to go! FOR CHECK-IN: For contact-less check-in, bring your smart phone to the event. IN ORDER TO PARTICIPATE YOU MUST COMPLETE A LIABILITY WAIVER HERE. You will not be allowed to participate without this form signed. Please do this when you RSVP/sign up so we can save time for cleaning on the day of the event! Recycling is encouraged! We would love for you to separate out any aluminum cans, glass bottles or plastic bottles that you find, as these are all accepted materials. Supplies you can bring: 🦈 Reusable water bottle with water (no single-use plastic bottles!) 🦈 Reef-safe Sunscreen (make sure oxybenzone is NOT on the active ingredients list!) 🦈 Comfortable shoes 🦈 Download the app Marine Debris Tracker, and click here for a quick tutorial on how to use the app, and get ready to utilize the Marine Debris Tracker App to help create a bigger picture of marine debris and plastic pollution through collecting open data, generating scientific findings, informing policy, and inspiring upstream design. *You can earn extra community service hours by participating! 🦈 Follow and monitor our Instagram page, @seakeepers for updates! We will provide: 🦈 Garbage bags 🦈 Reusable gloves 🦈 Hand Sanitizer 🦈 Extra water 🦈 Community Service Hours / Service Learning Hours Please note, the cleanup is 2 hours long, so that is how many hours we will give for community service. However, if you use the Marine Debris Tracker to record trash data, we will give you FIVE hours! Marine debris isn’t an ocean problem – it’s a people problem. Be part of the solution! ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Parking: Park in lot 7 (the first lot on your left as you enter, or the last lot on your right as you exit) near the kayak launch. Cancellation or Postponing: Cleanup will proceed as scheduled rain or shine, and cleanups will only be affected by the presence of lightning. Any extreme or hazardous weather will be monitored closely and the final call will be made to cancel or postpone a cleanup 2 hours prior to the start of the cleanup. For example, a 9am cleanup that is being postponed due to weather will be cancelled at 7am. Volunteers will be notified by email.

Title: Baynanza Central Dade
Content:
Baynanza is a celebration of Biscayne Bay and its significance as one of the most important ecological systems in South Florida. Celebrated throughout March and April, Baynanza culminates with the Biscayne Bay Cleanup Day where thousands of volunteers join together to help clean up our bay’s shoreline.

The 42nd annual Baynanza Biscayne Bay Cleanup Day will take place on Saturday, April 13, from 9 a.m. to noon. Sign up to celebrate our incredible marine resources and help restore the Biscayne Bay watershed at over 30 locations across Miami-Dade County. Registered volunteers at all cleanup sites will receive a free commemorative T-shirt. Community service hours are available to all students who participate.

Find and Register for Cleanups on the County's website here: https://www.miamidade.gov/global/service.page?Mduid_service=ser1516206542736138

Title: Beach Squad Beach Cleanup - Daytona Beach, Florida
Content:
Register for any beach cleanup you would like for free through our Eventbrite link below:

Click Here To Register For Beach Squad Beach Cleanups
 

EVENT DETAILS:

LOCATION:

Sun Splash Park

611 S Atlantic Ave, Daytona Beach, FL 32118

-To find our Cleanup Station, head to the beach in front of the Sun Splash Parking Lot. Look for the red ‘Cleanup’ flag and red cleanup buckets next to our Beach Squad cleanup station. You can get to the beach by using the stairs or ramp from the parking lot.

 

SIGN-UP: Each volunteer registers for the event at Eventbrite.com with their individual email. (CLICK HERE TO REGISTER FOR A CLEANUP)

-On the day of the cleanup, all volunteers sign their names after reviewing and accepting the waiver form.

-Adults registering for the cleanup can also register up to 4 minors or individuals without email addresses. The registering adult assumes all responsibility and liability for any volunteers they register.

 

PARKING: The Sun Splash Parking lot, located directly behind the Beach Squad Beach Cleanup Tent, offers paid parking.

Volusia County residents with proof of residency can park for free.

-Free parking is also available on the side streets surrounding Sun Splash Park. Please avoid parking in areas marked ‘no parking’.

 

WHAT TO BRING:

1) Water: Reusable water bottle filled with drinking water

 

2) Your Favorite Sun protection:

-Ocean-friendly sunscreen

-UV-protective long-sleeve

shirt

-Hat

-Sunglasses

 

3) Footwear (optional): Sandals or shoes to protect your feet from debris

 

4) Most importantly: Your positive energy!

 

PROVIDED: Beach Squad provides buckets, pickers, gloves, and trash bags for volunteers to use during the cleanup.

*Buckets and pickers need to be returned to the Beach Squad Cleanup Station by 10:45am.

 

END OF CLEANUP: After the cleanup event, we will weigh the trash collected by each volunteer and take a photo of you with your contributions if you would like!

We encourage you to tag us and brag about your accomplishments with your friends on social media!

Title: KEY BISCAYNE COMMUNITY CLEANUP
Content:
Join the Village of Key Biscayne and FillABag for an all ages community cleanup on March 1, 2025 from 9:30AM-12:30PM.  Children 12 and under must be accompanied by an adult.   • 12:10-12:30PM; Weigh In

Title: Haulover Park Coastal Cleanup (1st Saturday)
Content:
On the first Saturday of every month, volunteers can assist the Haulover Park staff and beautify this coastal park to keep our ocean ecosystem healthy. Volunteers will also get an opportunity to learn about their impact on local wildlife.

This volunteer opportunity is made possible with the support of our community partner, Miami-Dade County Sea Turtle Conservation Program (STCP). The STCP works to protect our sea turtle nests on 19 miles of Miami beaches during nesting season (March-October). STCP is committed to protecting our coastal and ocean ecosystems year-round, and educating the public on best conservation practices. Join STCP team members at our monthly coastal cleanups to learn more about the endangered sea turtle species that utilize our local ecosystems.

Responsibilities and Duties:

- Removing microplastics and trash
- Additional tasks as needed
Qualifications: Youth under 15 must have a parent/guardian present.

Commitment Expected: Please arrive at your scheduled start time and check-in with Sea Turtle staff. Please bring a refillable water bottle, closed-toed shoes, and protection from the sun (sunscreen, hats, sunglasses). If you have your own gloves, we recommend bringing them. Community service hours letters will be emailed, by request, following the event.

If you would like to participate in this event, please register on ParkLink in advance.

On the fourth Sunday of every month, volunteers can assist the Causeway staff and beautify this coastal park to keep our ocean ecosystem healthy. Gloves and trash bags will be provided, but volunteers are encouraged to bring their own reusable gloves to reduce waste.

Responsibilities and Duties:

- Removing microplastics and trash along the Green Space Park on Venetian Causeway's shoreline
- Additional tasks as needed
Qualifications: Youth under 15 must have a parent/guardian present.

Commitment Expected: Please arrive at your scheduled start time and check-in with park staff. Please bring a refillable water bottle, closed-toed shoes, and protection from the sun (sunscreen, hats, sunglasses). If you have your own gloves, we recommend bringing them. Community service hours letters will be emailed, by request, following the event.

If you would like to participate in this event, please register on ParkLink in advance.

Title: Community Action Day @ Fruit & Spice (Last Sunday)
Content:
Join us on the last Sunday of every month for a day of fun & light gardening at the Fruit & Spice Park! Volunteers will help with weeding the herb & vegetable garden and the more than 150 fruit tree seedlings kept in their tropical climate greenhouse. The herb & vegetable garden features crops like tomatoes and potatoes, lovingly tended by dedicated volunteers and staff. By supporting the garden we ensure there is a space for everyone to benefit from the knowledge imparted by the study of Ethnobotany, how plants and people affect each other!

Responsibilities and Duties:

- Light gardening and mulching
- Removing vines and weeds
- Additional tasks as needed
Qualifications: All ages are welcome. Must be able to bend for extended periods of time and able to work outdoors for up to 3 hours.

Commitment Expected: Please arrive on time and check-in with staff. We recommend having sunscreen & bug spray, a hat & comfortable clothing for warm temperature, and a reusable water bottle.

If you would like to participate in this event, please register on ParkLink in advance.

Title: The Monthly Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep
Content:
The Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep takes place every second Saturday of the month from 8 am – 11 am at Las Olas Blvd and A1A.  You can join us any month you like.  If you are part of a group just let us know how many attendees you expect.  For groups we can set up tents and tables.  We provide pickers and buckets for the cleanup.  

We provide Community Service Hours. 

The Fort Lauderdale Beach Sweep together with The City of Fort Lauderdale Neighbor Volunteer Office, and the Rotary Community Corps sponsors this monthly event To Keep Fort Lauderdale Beach Beautiful And Protect The Local Wild Life!

The City of Fort Lauderdale Parks and Recreation Department is doing an awesome job at keeping our beaches in pristine condition. Their equipment does not pick up small items such as cigarette butts, can tabs, and bottle caps.  Volunteers typically collect 100 pounds of trash, 25 pounds of recyclables and 7,000 cigarette butts.  You can help protect our jewel of Fort Lauderdale Beach and local wild life by removing these serious threats to sea gulls, turtles …our beach and ocean environment.

Volunteers meet and register at 300 S Fort Lauderdale Beach Boulevard, where East Las Olas Blvd. meets the beach.  There is volunteer parking at the Las Olas Garage, 200 Las Olas Circle (Las Olas and the east side of the Intracoastal Waterway) ON THE 3rd FLOOR ONLY, UNTIL NOON.  Cars will be ticketed with no recourse if parking instructions are not exactly followed.

Important Volunteer Information:

Please participate responsibly, especially if you have allergies or special needs.

• Proper attire is closed toed shoes and comfortable clothing - things you do not mind getting dirty! 

• Due to the outdoor activity, it is recommended all volunteers wear a hat, sunscreen, and insect repellent, plus bring their own water and snacks. Stay hydrated!

 

• All tools will be provided; but if you feel more comfortable with your own gloves and protective equipment, please bring them.

 

Let us know if you need anything else.

Title: Mad Beach Amphibious Trash & Ghost Crab Trap Round Up
Content:

With your help, we can make a tangible difference in preserving the beauty and health of our aquatic environments. Join us for a fun and rewarding day of cleaning up the streets of Little Havana while learning about its rich history and culture with Caro the Tour Guide. The project gets community members involved in environmental activities that protect communities from the effects of heat, pollution, and flooding. Organizations including The CLEO Institute, Miami Waterkeeper, Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science, Rescue a Reef, and Debris Free Oceans are coming together to provide access to opportunities across Miami-Dade. Content:
Join us on Friday Oct 31, 2025, at 9:00 AM at the Lowry Park Boat Ramp for a spooktacular event that combines cleaning up our environment with some sweet treats!

Don't forget to wear comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes. We'll provide all the cleaning supplies, so just bring yourself and a positive attitude!

Come join us for a day of **cleaning**, **fun**, and **treats** at Hallo-Clean 2025!

Hallo-Clean

Is an annual event that Keep Tampa Bay Beautiful hosts to encourage our community to celebrate Halloween in an environmentally conscious way. Americans buy about 600 million pounds of candy for this holiday and most candy wrappers are not recyclable. It is important to properly dispose of trash especially micro-trash like candy wrappers, because it is harder to collect smaller pieces of litter once it makes its way to our roadways, parks, and shorelines!

Title: Miami Beach Cleanup with The Palms Hotel & Spa ICC2025
Content:
Join us for the world's largest, one-day volunteer effort for our oceans and waterways, and show your commitment to reducing marine debris, along with millions of volunteers from across the globe! Lend a hand in raising awareness of microplastics and other debris that litters our wonderful beaches while doing your part in mitigating the impact on our coastal city. Meet us right behind The Palms Hotel & Spa on the beach! We will provide garbage bags, gloves, data collection cards, and a souvenir tote bag with this year’s marine animal theme! *Community Service hours also provided. Registration + waivers are required to participate.*

  • You can complete the online waivers in advance to help expedite check-in on the day of.
  • However, if you are under 18 and coming without a parent or guardian, you must have a parent/guardian print and sign the waiver HERE in advance, and bring it with you to the cleanup.

Important details:

  • Download the Ocean Conservancy’s CleanSwell app to participate in the Citizen Science activity to log, tally and measure the impact of your cleanup.
  • Dress for the weather and wear appropriate footwear. This is a beach site and while wearing flip flops or being barefoot is ok, we always recommend water shoes or closed toe shoes, since there are rocky areas to clean as well.
  • Sunglasses, hat, and sunscreen and recommended.
  • If you have your own reusable working or gardening type gloves, bring them. We will be providing gloves but cannot guarantee they will be in your size.
  • Some volunteers like to use a bucket during a cleanup. We have several buckets to lend you, but you can always ask your local Chinese, Burger or Bakery/Donut shop if they get food service items in 5-gallon buckets that they would like to donate for use during your cleanup!
  • Please bring water in a reusable container. Let’s reduce waste and refuse single-use disposable plastic water bottles.
  • On-street parking could be available on the streets around the hotel and there are public lots on 28th and 35th Streets.
  • Valet parking at the hotel is $29 + tax unless you decide to stay for brunch at Essensia restaurant (we are offering a great Miami Spice Brunch Menu!) and then it can be validated for $19 + tax.

Read more about the history and impact of the International Coastal Cleanup.
